# Intelligent Prism UI Design System

Version: 1.13.1
Status: Canonical design-system baseline
Language: zh-CN
Site: https://intelligence-prism-ui.ashrvm.chatgpt.site/
Repository: https://github.com/Ashrum/intelligence-prism-ui
Base: coss UI @ e937becd2d5ffb5c621eed6f8b1f223cbb6051e7

## Purpose
Intelligent Prism (智能曜彩) is the canonical UI design system for OLE product interfaces. This file is the discovery and authority entry point for web-capable agents. It does not replace the human-facing site.

## Authority
When sources differ, use this order:
1. Intelligent Prism component specification and Agent Spec on the relevant component page.
2. Intelligent Prism Foundations.
3. Intelligent Prism reusable patterns and application examples.
4. Pinned coss upstream behavior.
5. Agent inference.

Application examples demonstrate composition and do not override component specifications. Agent inference must never override an existing specification.

If a required rule is absent:
1. Reuse the pinned coss behavior when applicable.
2. If coss does not define it, report the specification gap.
3. Do not invent visual values, component behavior, or a replacement design system.

## Canonical form-label rule
The canonical base form strategy is a persistent fixed label. Field identity remains visible in default, filled, error, readonly, and disabled states. Floating labels are not a base Input/Field behavior. A product may use a separately specified specialized pattern only when that pattern is explicitly documented; do not infer one.

## Agent reading instructions
- Read Foundations and only the component specifications relevant to the task.
- Preserve existing component behavior and semantic roles.
- Preserve established semantic color meanings. The scoped Expression v0.1 review permits non-semantic brand geometry for recognition; it must not encode task status or override component specifications.
- Do not infer pixel values from screenshots when the specification or source is available.
- When a visual value is not exposed by the page, inspect the linked source or pinned coss implementation before reporting a gap.
- Keep accessibility semantics, keyboard behavior, theme behavior, and reduced-motion support intact.
- Do not turn application examples into new generic components.


## Page composition layers (candidate branch)
- Page skeleton catalog: /next/skeletons
- Teacher workbench shell review: /next/skeletons/workbench (v0.3 Candidate; fixtures only)
- Standard pages: /next/pages (not started)
Skeletons and standard pages are separate categories and do not change the 80-component count. Compose the same WorkbenchShell source in applications. Stage 1 and the authorized stage 2 Agent skeleton are review candidates; stages 3–7 remain unstarted. Review fixtures are not production services.

- Agent page skeleton review: /next/skeletons/agent (v0.1 Candidate; same WorkbenchShell and AgentComposer; local fixtures only)

- AI activity monitor: components/prism-next/skeletons/ai-activity-monitor.tsx. Current-user grading/parsing records only; state, trustworthy counts and follow-up are distinct. Review fixture includes nine scenes and explicit manual advancement; no live tasks.

## Teacher use cases and parsing workflow (v0.1 Candidate)
- Teacher use cases: /next/use-cases (7 primary goals, 6 parsing scenarios, exception paths and acceptance points).
- Parsing workflow: /next/use-cases/parsing (query case=single|images|pdf|scan|answers|student).
- Business use cases are not generic components or approved standard pages. Reuse WorkbenchShell and Prism/coss source.
- Fixed local fixtures only. Actual selected files are not uploaded or parsed; image previews and PDF metadata only. No OCR, scanner, grading, publishing or production question-bank integration.
- Review, execution and saving are distinct. Missing cross-page sources block save. Confirmed snapshots are isolated from later drafts. Word/Excel remain Step2.

Typography: /next/foundations/typography (v0.2.1 implementation candidate)
Use semantic text roles; reading and long editing 16/28, decision hints >=14px. Theme and task state never shrink typography. Keep vendored coss sources unchanged; include the Prism typography adaptation stylesheet.

## Expression review v0.1 (Candidate)
- Entry: /next/foundations#expression-review
- Three samples on existing pages: Agent welcome (/next/skeletons/agent); material intake and saved results (/next/use-cases/parsing); warm-paper categorical and sequential colors (/next/components/status-composition and /next/components/evidence-matrix).
- Original/candidate controls preserve drafts, task state and selected data. Global theme tokens, brand names/colors, typography roles and coss source remain unchanged.
- This is a scoped review, not a new global visual default or a full-site re-audit. Real device and color-vision simulation are not included in this round.
- Heatmap sequentialColors accepts three six-digit opaque HEX colors in low/mid/high order. Labels choose black/white against the interpolated fill; hover preserves fill and emphasizes the border.

## Guided Agent tasks v0.1.1 (Candidate)
- Reusable patterns: /next/components/agent-components. Composer, clarification, context references, execution rows and change review are controlled components; the caller owns business state, execution and persistence.
- Complete example: /next/agent, trial-paper parsing tab. Reuses the exact ParsingWorkspace/reducer shown at /next/use-cases/parsing, including source inspection, failure retry, review and local sample saving. The material-review assistant remains available in its tab and compact reading integration.
- Interaction reference: https://www.beautifului.dev/ (Approval Card, Context Cards, Task Rows, Diff Table). Prism / coss implementation; no copied Beautiful UI code, dependency or imported visual system.
- Selection does not execute a task. Accepted changes are not saved/published; reject stale proposals and require renewed checking. Additional requirements appear in the reusable task instruction; editing its copy does not mutate the task.
- Fixed fixtures only. Actual file content is not parsed; no OCR/model/backend grading or publishing. No fabricated confidence, progress percentage or reasoning traces.

- DraftMathPreview renders the CURRENT stem/answer with pinned Temml 0.13.4 into native MathML / existing STIX. Conservative Unicode algebra and explicit \(…\) / \[ … \] are supported; unrecognized prose and invalid formulas preserve input. Rendering checks layout syntax, never mathematical correctness; no write-back, source edits or automatic confirmation. Length/expansion limits and untrusted-mode rendering apply.
- Shared step badges stay 14px; loading uses the existing Spinner with reduced-motion support. Review code: https://github.com/Ashrum/intelligence-prism-ui/pull/18 (candidate branch, not main).

## Agent semantic group v0.1 (Design candidate, 2026-09-22)
- Entry: /next/components/agent-components#context-summary-review. Six independent semantics plus a confirmation/progress/result composition; two manual fixture purposes. Catalog stays at 80 entries. See docs/agent-context-summary-review.md.
- Reuse AgentContextSummary, AgentContextList, AgentChangeReview and AgentTaskProgress. Add controlled AgentArtifactPreview, AgentExecutionConfirmation, AgentExecutionProgress and AgentExecutionResult in agent-semantic-components.tsx. No business page, store, authorization engine or Runtime is added.
- Context selection, read, current-context and citation remain independent host facts. Absent requires complete event coverage; unknown and unavailable are distinct. Source inspection does not update facts.
- Preview title/version/status/summary and open capability are external; no capability means no invented open action. Confirmation only exposes submission in ready state; submitting, received, blocked, recorded and unknown are distinct. Callbacks are intents, never receipts.
- Overall progress does not derive from steps. Waiting or unknown stops live animation and labels the last running step as a snapshot. No percentages or timers.
- Result receipts distinguish succeeded/partial/failed/unknown. Unknown accepts query only; partial retains completed and remaining scope. Generated, reviewable and published are separate facts.
- ChangeReview adds optional version labels, scope, preview slots and reset callback; legacy string input is preserved. The caller rejects stale proposals, owns the decision/draft and saves separately. Preview slots are not semantic diff engines.
- Source and acceptance are scoped to the Site candidate; this does not imply a GitHub main merge or Workspace/real-service acceptance.
